text:
sam: Quick heads-up — EU infra trending weird ahead of the holiday week. we're getting a lot more long-context streaming sessions and it's hitting eu-west pools.

nisha: details? any hard numbers?

sam: short list: 1) 48h rolling GPU hours for eu-west p4d pool are +2.6x vs baseline. 2) tail latency (95p) for short routes bumped 320ms -> 520ms. 3) KV cache hit rate for streaming is up ~8% (good), but overall throughput is down ~12% because per-request token counts and memory pressure.

ben: network noise vs memory/compute saturation? seeing OOMs?

sam: no OOMs in logs, but NVLink utilization and cross-rack fabric show spikes during streaming bursts. netmon shows intermittent packet drops on a 10Gb uplink between racks around peak windows.

olivia: product context: a couple enterprise customers turned on continuous streaming for large documents (~1e5 tokens/session) for a localized marketing push in EU. they expect elevated traffic for ~2 weeks.

capacity-bot: predicted_peak_gpu_hours: 4200 (window: next 72h).

nisha: proposal: pre-warm +8 p4d nodes in eu-west for 12 days, enable more aggressive KV prefix caching for streaming routes, and enforce a soft 65k context cap on hosted free tier during the window. rough cost est ~USD 17.6k.

ben: alternative: gate long-context customers into Dedicated/dedicated-reserved pool for the campaign. reduces host-tier impact.

olivia: that would need account migrations/consent. some of those customers have region/data constraints, so moving them off eu-west isn't trivial.

sam: actionables I suggest:
- eng-infra: schedule pre-warm (start in ~6h) and run a canary replay of last 24h traffic scaled x3.
- eng-runtime: bump KV cache memory threshold + collect miss/hit histograms by route.
- product: notify top-5 affected customers about voluntary migration or temporary soft limits.

nisha: I'll post the cost breakdown to #finance and confirm budget. If finance approves, we proceed with pre-warm.

ben: if fabric packet drops persist after pre-warm, we should consider moving some nodes to a different AZ or adding cross-rack bandwidth (short-term cross-connect). need SRE signoff for network ops.

sam: I'll attach netmon captures and quick runbook. also adding a simple traffic-shaper to reduce concurrency per-hosted-instance as a fall-back.

olivia: product: no objections to pre-warm. we'll draft customer comms for voluntary migration.

nisha: no objections from me either. will ping finance now.

sam: kicking off pre-warm job now (creating instances + warming caches). I'll update this thread with timing and any canary results.

ben: thanks — please include the exact instance IDs in the update so infra can trace network paths.

sam: will do.
